note: DEMO CONTENT, DERIVED by research-agent on 2026-11-12. No frozen delivery baseline exists (.mw/metrics/ is empty) and no delivery history exists (GAP-006 waived), so both ranges are judgement from the size measures below, not calibrated. Person-days count human effort (review, decisions, gates, pairing); agent compute time is not counted.
basis: Size, STATED in research/inputs/baseline-metrics.md: 2,123 Python source lines, 6 capabilities, 82 business rules, 54 test functions; and from the code at e1fbd3a: 40 HTTP endpoints, 5 enum types, 1 SQLite database
Behaviour is already specified: the confirmed baseline has a rules-trace per capability and all 21 open questions answered or deferred, so discovery effort is not in either range

Traditional (DERIVED): a Rust engineer rewriting a FastAPI and SQLAlchemy service typically produces 3,000 to 5,000 lines of Rust for 2,000 lines of Python; at roughly 100 to 150 reviewed lines a day plus a parity harness (5 to 8 days), data-compatibility work (4 to 8 days) and new parity tests for rules that no existing Python test covers (count unmeasured, RISK-004) gives 35 to 60 person-days

Agentic (DERIVED): agents draft the specs, parity tests and Rust code per capability from the rules-trace; human effort goes to the gates (research, PRD, plan, PR reviews), the Rust platform ADR (DEP-003), the data-compatibility review (ASM-002) and fixing parity failures that need judgement. Estimated at 2 to 4 human days per capability (6 capabilities) plus 0 to 1 day of fixed overhead

Six capabilities can be built in waves along the baseline's dependency order (Accounts first, then Following, then Posting, Timelines, Notifications, Moderation), which bounds the high end for both approaches

change-sizing (DERIVED): this is not a same-day change; at major classification it should be split into at least one story per capability plus a platform story (app wiring, errors, config, data layer) and a parity-harness story

widening.GAP-006: No delivery history and no frozen .mw/metrics/baseline.json: no calibration, so both ranges are wide (high is about 2x low)
widening.GAP-004: No incident history: unknown edge cases in existing data could add data-compatibility work (DEP-005)
widening.RISK-003: Framework-level behaviour (validation error bodies, JSON formats) is not specified; deciding and matching it could add 2 to 5 days to either range
widening.DEP-003: Rust stack not chosen yet; an unfamiliar framework or driver would push both ranges toward the high end
